question: What does update_tools([]) do to an agent's tool set?
options: It removes all tools including those defined on the agent class
It adds an empty toolset to the existing tools
It removes all dynamically added tools, but tools defined as decorated methods on the class are not affected
It resets the tools to the original set from the constructor
explanation: update_tools() replaces the dynamic tool list. Passing an empty list removes all dynamically added tools. However, tools defined as decorated methods on the agent class are not affected by update_tools() and remain available.

question: When should you use dynamic tools instead of an agent handoff?
options: When the conversation needs a fundamentally different personality
When the agent's tone and role stay the same but its available actions change
When the user explicitly asks to speak to a different agent
When you need to reinitialize state and reset conversation context
explanation: Dynamic tools are best when the agent's personality stays the same but its capabilities change, like moving from an ordering phase to a payment phase within the same Order Taker agent. Agent handoffs are better when the conversation needs a fundamentally different tone or role. The restaurant system uses both: handoffs between agents and dynamic tools within the Order Taker.

question: Why does update_instructions() replace the entire system prompt rather than appending to it?
options: Because appending would cause the prompt to grow unboundedly
Because the LLM can only process one system message at a time
Because a complete replacement is predictable and easy to debug, since each phase has a self-contained instruction set
Because LiveKit does not support incremental prompt updates
explanation: Replacing the entire prompt makes behavior predictable and debuggable. Each phase has a complete, self-contained instruction set that you can read independently. Incremental patching would create complex interactions between old and new instructions, making bugs harder to track down.
